newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico profit drop reflects copper prices.
newsitem.headline: GMexico profit drop reflects copper prices.

text.p: Mexican mining company Grupo Mexico SA's 1996 results held no surprises, analysts said on Friday, as a slump in copper prices cast a shadow over the year's earnings.
The nation's largest mining firm reported 1996 net profits of 2.57 billion pesos versus 4.60 billion pesos the previous year.
Earnings per share dropped to 3.73 pesos in 1996 from 6.68 pesos in 1995, below a forecast of 3.87 pesos per share of three analysts surveyed by Reuters.
Profits were hurt by slumping revenues, which fell to 9.875 billion pesos from 12.866 billion pesos during 1995.
On the upside, copper prices on the futures markets appear to be on the rebound, analysts said, and the company has succeeded in increasing its margins.
"You can see the efforts the company is making in strict control of expenses," Merrill Lynch Mexico City analyst Jose Buendia said.
He said operating margins rose in the fourth quarter to 30.7 percent from 13.0 percent in the third quarter.
Valores Finamex brokerage analyst Chris Albi also noted the company's margins are "pretty healthy," but that the company is holding a lot of cash.
"The company is still boxed in because of the Asarco stalemate," he said.

Albi added that the GMexico cannot declare a dividend until it reaches an agreement with U.S. based-ASARCO Inc to buy back 105 million shares of its own shares, a stake of almost 23 percent in GMexico. The two companies have agreed on a buyback of the stake and are said to be in negotiations.
